designStatus: Original untested source-fit protocols; no learner observations or private state changes

tasks: Use the applicable reliable local healthy-eating guide to sort foods, distinguish food groups from nutrients and plan a varied day of meals; retain all Qh whole-card nutrient/body-function checks.
Actually prepare a simple chosen snack using washing, peeling/tearing/spreading, appropriate cutting and combining; retain hand/surface hygiene, cold-food care and allergy checks.

Serve a modest initial portion with an option for more, attend to hunger/appetite and plan safe use/storage/disposal of leftovers. Food stewardship is assessed without requiring a cleaned plate or shaming a food preference.

Compare a beneficial food-choice explanation with a genuine hygiene/allergy/unsafe-food risk; do not teach that one food categorically causes disease or transfer adult quantitative dietary prescriptions to a child.

Use a checked age-appropriate local guide case with mixed dishes and qualitative group proportions. NIN reference-child diagrams are examples with declared assumptions, not individual prescriptions; no adult energy/fluid quantities, calorie counting or body-weight target is transplanted into a child task.
protocols.sourceContextualChannel: Formal liking is retained separately from knowledge/skill and meal stewardship. Correct performance does not prove positive feeling; no forced tasting or enthusiasm.

resourceBasis.use: Food-group/nutrient distinction, varied meals and qualified reference-child examples; individual amounts/weights not assessed or prescribed.

tasks: Use the complete existing hygiene task design: handwashing with soap, toothbrushing, cough/sneeze hygiene and ordinary bathing/self-care routines, with appropriate privacy and materials.
Use a suitable water container, cup and serving utensil to obtain/serve a small amount without spilling; include changed container/utensil transfer rather than assume this from snack choice.
Communicate an ordinary unwell feeling to an appropriate adult and ask for practical help; do not substitute emotion-vocabulary accuracy or require diagnosis.
protocols.taskFitBoundary: Use the serving component as a contribution while retaining the exact actual water/utensil/no-spill duty in the source task. No new per-container mastery state or inference from snack-only performance is introduced.
protocols.guideBoundary: Do not import the legacy body-parts guide’s optional blindfold/nose-pinching/raw-food test. Canonical organ naming/mapping and actual basic hygiene remain; no such extra demonstration is required for protective-help or self-care coverage.

tasks: Actually care for school books, study materials and furniture: handle them without avoidable damage, restore their assigned storage and explain/demonstrate an appropriate care adjustment. Food-workbench success alone does not prove care of a borrowed book.

Complete an appropriate teacher-supervised cleanup task across the declared classroom/play/bathroom handwashing-area cases using suitable materials and responsibilities. Retain actual clearing, cleaning and organisation, not just saying that rules matter.

Use safe selected samples to carry out the printed wet/dry sorting case. Use the locally supplied current disposal chart separately; wet/dry does not exhaust every possible waste stream or mean simply recyclable/non-recyclable.

Retain complete food-workspace hygiene, craft material/tool care and safe storage, fair group work and a separate full sorting/count/order check. Wet/dry classification alone does not establish the counting component.

currentResourceBasis.use: Current resource distinguishes additional disposal streams; use a safe wet/dry sample exercise without an exhaustive two-bin assertion. No legal compliance lesson or new source catalogue ingestion.

tasks: Use suitable craft scissors and a child-safe soft-food knife in actual work, retaining complete Ft cutting/joining/shaping and F62 food-preparation/hygiene checks. No firmer-vegetable bridge/claw inventory is imposed merely because the source lists a small knife.

Demonstrate selecting, carrying, controlling and storing suitable tools. A taught nail-care tool case remains a source-specific practical condition where applicable; saying a safety rule is insufficient.
Independent action means the learner performs without step-by-step prompting; adult supervision/provision remains compatible with that condition and is not withdrawn to create independence.
Use actual local road signs/rules in a protected simulation and a suitably supervised familiar walk: choose where to walk, identify a crossing, stop/look/check and seek appropriate help.
Interpret a changed safety-symbol case and act on it; unfamiliar signs are supplied/taught rather than assumed to belong to every locality.
Retain the complete everyday-safety and sign claims; no new cycling-skill node is implied by an illustrative cycling example.
protocols.intrinsicBoundary: The book-classification dependency is supportive rather than necessary; full sign interpretation and practical action remain required.

tasks: Use non-graphic supplied scenarios to distinguish necessary care from touching that is not OK, identify trusted adults beyond parents and rehearse a protective report.
Retain the complete body-ownership, early-warning, asking-help and no/go/tell chains, including that freezing or inability to leave is never the child’s fault and they can keep telling.
Explain a relevant rule consequence and practise a safe response to an offered gift/unknown person; do not imply known people cannot be unsafe or transfer responsibility for abuse onto a child.
Plan a manageable health/safety routine, specify context and materials, track and reflect on its implementation design and support another person where appropriate.
Bring together meal/self-care, shared-space care, appropriate tools and protective-help tasks; goal coverage is reviewed independently rather than inferred by summing child-code labels.
protocols.authoringBoundary: This specifies future evidence collection; it does not manufacture a week of child observations, declare a learner competent or change learner state.
